proposal.name: Define repository checks from a committed base

plan.name: Define repository checks from a committed base
plan.summary: Add a version 1 .invariant/repository.json contract and a shared internal/repository loader for Go, Python and TypeScript parts, with digest-pinned images, explicit dependency inputs, argument-array commands and reasons for inapplicable checks, using the format and API specified by the acceptance tests. Capture a caller-supplied committed base revision and expose its configuration, file contents, trust declarations and applicable parts without consulting candidate files or executing repository commands; reject malformed declarations, unsafe paths and ambiguous ownership. Select checks deterministically for existing, new and deleted paths using the deepest enclosing part plus declared sharing and dependency consumers, select all parts for repository configuration and agent/current-state documents, and reject any unowned touched path. Keep the existing Invariant plumbing runner, commands, sandbox limits, scope rules and modeled-project manifests as the explicit compatibility path, keep external plumbing disabled, and add the new loader and repository configuration to Invariant's trusted base. Update SPEC.md with the delivered behavior and its existing decision foundations (D-0105, D-0109, D-0121 and D-0122), add a short README pointer within its 400-line limit, and document the format, ownership, base authority and compatibility boundary in docs/factory.md; the merger must record this step's new repository-contract decision before the next step, since the build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestRepositoryContractLanguages
tests.says: Version 1 single-part Go, Python and TypeScript contracts and a mixed Go/TypeScript contract load from a commit and preserve their declared commands, inputs and documentation paths.

tests.name: TestRepositoryContractMissingIsDistinct
tests.says: An absent committed repository contract has a distinct error from malformed declarations and invalid base revisions, and a candidate-only contract never supplies missing base authority.

tests.name: TestRepositoryContractRejectsInvalidDeclarations
tests.says: Unsupported versions and languages, mutable images, incomplete or contradictory commands, unknown or duplicate JSON fields, missing dependency declarations and ambiguous owners are rejected with useful diagnostics.

tests.name: TestRepositoryContractRejectsUnsafePaths
tests.says: Declarations and touched paths cannot escape the repository, traverse committed links or submodules, or name Git metadata; required inputs and documents must be committed regular files.

tests.name: TestRepositoryContractKeepsBaseAuthority
tests.says: Editing or committing a candidate configuration, moving the base ref and mutating returned values cannot replace captured commands, input and rule bytes, ownership or trust.

tests.name: TestRepositoryContractOwnsEveryTouchedPath
tests.says: Nested parts, shared files and workspace dependency inputs select a stable deduplicated set of applicable parts, including for planned additions and deletions, and any unowned path fails the whole selection.

tests.name: TestRepositoryContractLeavesModeledProjectsSeparate
tests.says: Modeled-project manifests continue to load without repository configuration, are never mistaken for it, and can coexist with a repository contract.

tests.name: TestRepositoryAuthorityIsInInvariantsTrustedBase
tests.says: Invariant protects the new loader and repository contract alongside every existing trusted path while retaining its existing plan ownership, regression-test allowance and sandbox budgets.

usage.summary: Wrote `plan.json` and eight acceptance tests covering base authority, validation, ownership, compatibility, and documentation. The first check passed: all eight tests fail on the current code, and `repo/` remains unchanged.
